Since 1.5.7-17, zstd-jni is a multi-release JAR: on JDK 22+, its stream classes
(ZstdInputStreamNoFinalizer, ZstdOutputStreamNoFinalizer, the buffer streams) come from
META-INF/versions/22 and call libzstd through java.lang.foreign rather than JNI. The image
builder runs on JDK 25, so native images get that implementation, and every downcall it
makes has to be registered here, or the image throws MissingForeignRegistrationError when
The entries below are the distinct function descriptors of the downcall handles in
ZstdBinding types every size_t as the linker's canonical 'size_t' layout and pointers as
plain ValueLayout.ADDRESS, hence 'size_t' and 'void*' here. The 'critical' ones are linked
with Linker.Option.critical(true) so heap byte[]s can be passed as pointers, which changes
the generated stub, hence the option on those entries.
